description: WebGL unmasked vendor and renderer identity, conditioned on the resolved anchor. An option is either a MEASURED member of that anchor or an AUTHORED identity registered on it through its `member` block, which names the label the runtime reports and the measured member whose WebGPU adapter the identity carries. scripts/generate-dispersion-tables.py folds registered identities into the anchor's compiled member table and hard-fails if an offered identity is neither measured nor registered, so the runtime membership check in Compose can never see an identity the catalogue did not account for. Identity rotation is never valid across anchors: that is the failure the retired family catalogue shipped. The anchor a GPU-less host resolves is a HARDWARE anchor of the claimed platform, not the software one, so every default launch draws from a pool with per-seed entropy; see the swiftshader option set's note.
label: gpu_identity

options.note: Measured identity strings on anchor linux-swiftshader-google-6922d61bab83 (Linux / ANGLE/SwiftShader). Identity and capability agree: the string names SwiftShader and the cluster is what SwiftShader measured. Evidence is compatibility-capture, not physical-ground-truth, because the machine this describes is a host with no usable GPU device rather than any particular piece of hardware. NEVER DRAWN BY DEFAULT, on any host. Patch 0102 excludes the software anchor from the drawn candidate set: a host with no hardware backend draws a hardware anchor of the claimed platform instead, because there is no backend for a capability cluster to be coherent with and a self-identifying software-rasteriser string is the loudest value a page can read. This option is reachable only when the launch asks for it by name -- --fingerprint-anchor linux-swiftshader-google-6922d61bab83, or --fingerprint-gpu-renderer / --fingerprint-gpu-vendor narrowing the draw onto this one member. It is also the only single-member option set in this table, so drawing it offers no per-seed rotation, which is the second reason it is not a default.

options.note: Measured identity strings on anchor linux-vulkan-nvidia-adf287b8f0ee (Linux / ANGLE/Vulkan). Every member agrees on webgl1 caps, webgl2 caps and both render digests across Ampere, Ada and Blackwell silicon. WebGPU is NOT uniform here and travels with the member. Measured on Chromium 152.0.7977.82 against release pin 152.0.7977.83: same major, different patch. WEBGPU RESIDUAL, named because patch 0102 makes it reachable by default: this member measured NO WebGPU adapter, so the composed profile carries no webgpu fragment and navigator.gpu stays the host's. On a host with a real NVIDIA card that is the measurement reproduced exactly. On a GPU-less host it is not: measured through the shipped artifact under --use-angle=swiftshader, navigator.gpu.requestAdapter() returns an adapter whose info reads {vendor: "google", architecture: "swiftshader"}, so this identity would present a GeForce renderer string on WebGL beside a self-identifying software adapter on WebGPU -- one property read, no allocation. Claiming the sibling Ada members' nvidia/lovelace adapter here is refused for the reason the anchor states: this silicon is Ampere and Blackwell, lovelace would be a falsifiable unmeasured assertion. The nine Ada-bounded identities in this option set are unaffected, and so are all fifteen Windows and twelve Apple identities, whose anchors carry a full measured adapter with 36 limits. Reaching this needs --fingerprint-platform=linux, because the default persona on a Linux host is windows.

options.note: AUTHORED, NOT MEASURED. The renderer string's only variable slot is MTLDevice.name; the rest of the template is byte-identical to the measured Apple M4 Max string. The capability cluster behind this name is the measured M4 Max cluster. That this is the same surface a real machine with this chip produces is DERIVED FROM SOURCE, not measured: in third_party/angle/src/libANGLE/renderer/metal/DisplayMtl.mm, DisplayMtl::ensureCapsInitialized takes the TARGET_OS_OSX branch, where max2DTextureSize, maxVaryingVectors and maxVertexOutputComponents are literal constants and every other limit derives from them or from mtl:: constants; the only GPU-family predicates reachable on macOS are supportsAppleGPUFamily(1|3|4) and supportsEitherGPUFamily(2,1), all of which are true on every Apple silicon GPU because those report MTLGPUFamilyApple7 or later and Apple's families are cumulative. RESIDUAL: maxSamples comes from a device query (mFormatTable.getMaxSamples()); the anchor measured 4, which is the Apple silicon maximum. A real capture from this chip would replace this entry with physical-ground-truth.
options.source: Apple Mac technical specifications (support.apple.com); MTLDevice.name on Apple silicon is the marketed chip name, confirmed for Apple M4 Max by corpus/anchors/macos-metal-apple-850a91233555.json. Chip is presented only in machine classes Apple shipped it in.
